newsitem.title: FRANCE: Paris to promote French language in Louisiana.
newsitem.headline: Paris to promote French language in Louisiana.

text.p: France has renewed a two-year agreement to promote the French language in the U.S. state of Louisiana through teaching and television, the French Foreign Ministry said on Friday.

The new agreement with the public Council for the Development of the French Language provides for 25 primary school French teachers to be dispatched to the southern state, and reinforces the broadcasting of the TV5 French-language television channel beamed abroad.
It says French entertainers will visit Louisiana in 1999 for celebratons marking the 300th anniversary of the arrival of French settlers there.

The French colony, named after King Louis XIV, then extended from the Gulf of Mexico to Canada, comprising 10 modern U.S. states. Emperor Napoleon Bonaparte sold it to the United States in 1803 for 80 million francs of the time.
